conclusion: No quality or efficiency advantage was established. Delivered decision content scored 48/48 without retrieval, 47/48 with the same corpus flattened, and 48/48 with OpenAkashic structured references. The single flat error contradicted its own correct rationale, so it is not evidence of superior knowledge. Blind model explanation scores were 47/48, 45/48 and 45/48 respectively. Structured access used 52.2% more total provider tokens than no retrieval and 38.3% more than flat, with no explanation advantage. Strict requested-file scores were 42/48, 29/48 and 42/48; missing files are disclosed separately. These four selected tasks have a baseline ceiling and do not establish general usefulness or uselessness.

gates.reason: Base content ceiling, lower model rubric, higher token usage; one flat serialization inconsistency is not a knowledge advantage.

evidence_boundary: 4 tasks across 3 families with 2 repeats, not 48 independent cases
Curated version-specific documentation task families, not randomly sampled new production failures
Same-pool same-retriever flat baseline; no claim about all RAG or graph architectures
Final-response fallback analysis clarified during execution before content inspection; strict file results preserved
One anonymized model grader; no human evaluator and imperfect style blinding
Fresh agent state, not cold provider prefix cache; cached tokens included in input
Serial runs but shared host and provider response delays; no isolated performance inference
No output or rubric tuning, no failed candidate replacement
Independent upstream tests do not establish whole Streamlit UI or actual HTTP behavior

next_decision.adopt: Version, applicability, source and observed limits remain explicit; preserve measured failures and offline replay
next_decision.do_not_adopt: Mandatory retrieval as default or mass generic-document expansion based on a hoped-for benefit
next_decision.next_evidence_needed: Real public failure/application episodes with before/after state, context constraints, attempted alternatives and measurable outcomes; compare against same-information flat records before graph-value claims
